digest.en: Sitharaman and China’s foreign minister signaled readiness to address trade barriers, setting the tone for a cautious reset in bilateral relations. Simultaneously, Trump waived Graham Act sanctions on Russia before they took effect, a move that complicates Western pressure on Moscow.
digest.hi: चोरबागान की भगदड़ में 19 मौतों ने भीड़ प्रबंधन की नाकामी को उजागर किया है। इसी वक्त टेक्सास में स्कूली बच्चों के खिलाफ 47,000 क्रिमिनल केस दर्ज हो रहे हैं। दोनों घटनाओं में प्रशासनिक प्रतिक्रिया और न्यायिक प्रक्रिया के बीच स्पष्ट विरोधाभास दिखाई देता है।

articles.title: China says ready to address each other’s concerns after FM Sitharaman flags trade barriers
articles.summary: India’s trade deficit with China crossed 100 billion dollars in nine months. Finance Minister Sitharaman cited persistent market access barriers as a core concern. Beijing stated it is ready to address these issues through continued bilateral engagement. Reacting to India’s trade deficit with China crossing $100 billion in the first nine months, Nirmala Sitharaman said the growing trade imbalance and persistent restrictions on market access for Indian products remained major concerns, despite years of engagement with Beijing.

articles.title: Vice-President Vance faces tough questions on Iran war, immigration and more in CBS town hall
articles.summary: Vice-President Vance faced sharp questions on Iran, immigration, and policy failures during a CBS town hall. Several attendees admitted supporting Trump but criticized the administration’s record. The exchange highlighted potential challenges if he runs for president in 2028. The string of sharp queries, some from voters who said they had supported him and President Donald Trump, previewed the rocky path he may face trying to answer for the administration's record if he runs for President himself in 2028.

articles.title: ‘4,000 people minding our own business’: four decades on, Falklands again face a hostile Argentina
articles.summary: Argentina’s president is targeting the Falklands’ oil and fisheries industries amid declining poll numbers. Local residents and military police gathered in the islands’ legislative assembly. The move signals renewed hostility toward the British territory after four decades. Facing a slump in the polls, Argentina’s president is making economic attacks on the islands’ oil industry, and suggesting its key fisheries industry could be next A dozen local people and a uniformed military police officer (“Do you mind if I sit in?”) took their seats at the back of the handsome wood-panelled courtroom that doubles as the Falkland Islands’ legislative assembly.

articles.title: China considers new export curbs on solar, AI, biotech
articles.summary: China drafted a plan to ban exports of 14 technologies and restrict 26 others. The list includes next-generation solar and AI tools. India and other nations seeking to reduce reliance on Chinese supply chains face new hurdles. The draft plan, “Announcement No. 48”, proposes a complete export ban on 14 technologies and restrictions on 26 more, including next-generation solar technologies that could affect countries such as India seeking to reduce dependence on China.

articles.title: ‘Serious incident’ at Alberta military base causes deaths and injuries, Canada officials say
articles.summary: A large fire at the Wainwright military base in Alberta killed and injured multiple people. Hospitals in Edmonton reported being overwhelmed by the influx of casualties. Canada’s defence minister confirmed the incident as serious, with ongoing recovery efforts. Patients being taken to hospitals in Edmonton as Wainwright ‘completely overwhelmed’ by number of injuries, local doctor says People have been killed and injured after an incident at one of Canada’s busiest military training bases in Alberta caused a large fire, Canada’s defence minister said Saturday.“I’m saddened to share that there have been both fatalities and injuries as a result of an incide.

articles.title: Kasparov Says Talks With Putin Pointless, War Is 'Ideological Basis' Of His Rule
articles.summary: Garry Kasparov told RFE/RL that negotiations with Vladimir Putin are pointless. He argued the war serves as the ideological basis of Putin's rule. Kasparov dismissed a proposed US deal to purchase Russian diesel. He stated that a Ukrainian victory would likely end Putin's regime. Russian Chess grandmaster Garry Kasparov tells RFE/RL Putin is set on “liquidating Ukraine” and will not concessions.

articles.title: Flour sacks turned flood barriers: Gaza faces another winter without safe shelter
articles.summary: Families in the Gaza Strip are bracing for a winter of severe cold and rain that threatens to flood their remaining shelters. Ahmed Al-Omari and others are repurposing flour sacks as makeshift barriers against rising water. These improvised defenses highlight the lack of safe, durable housing in the war-ravaged territory. Residents continue to live in tattered tents and damaged buildings with no reliable protection from the elements. The situation underscores the ongoing humanitarian crisis as winter approaches.

articles.title: Russia's Deadly Attacks Damage Homes, Energy Sites In Ukraine As Kyiv Says Starlink Restrictions
articles.summary: Russia fired missiles and drones at Ukrainian cities on 17 October, killing at least twelve civilians and damaging residential blocks and power infrastructure. Russia continued to pound Ukraine with missiles and drones, killing civilians and damaging residential buildings and energy sites, as Kyiv described disruptions to the satellite communications of US company SpaceX, crucial to the country's defense, as a deliberate "operation.".

articles.title: Sanctions, War, Isolation: Why Hasn't Iran's Hard-Line Government Collapsed?
articles.summary: Iran's government has survived war, economic crisis, and protests due to entrenched power networks. A fractured opposition prevents unified resistance. Vahid Pourostad notes the system remains stable despite severe internal and external pressures. Iran’s Islamic republic has survived war, economic crisis, and widespread protests. So why is the system still standing? Vahid Pourostad of RFE/RL's Negah-e-Farda (Iran Tomorrow) program explains that its survival rests on entrenched networks of power and a fractured opposition.

articles.title: Trump Waives Graham Act Sanctions On Russia Before They Take Effect
articles.summary: Trump waived nearly all sanctions from the Graham Act before they took effect. The bipartisan law aimed to pressure Russia to end its war against Ukraine. The move prompted sharp criticism from Ukraine advocates. Lawmakers from both parties in the US condemned the decision. US President Donald Trump has waived nearly all substantive sanctions, tariffs, and restrictions included in a bipartisan law aimed at pressuring Russia to end its war against Ukraine, prompting sharp criticism from Ukraine advocates and US lawmakers from both parties.

articles.title: China, Russia quietly moving toward a new Arctic axis
articles.summary: Putin’s advisor Nikolai Patrushev visited China to advance Arctic cooperation. The talks focused on converting maritime agreements into durable infrastructure and logistics. This shift aims to build a resilient axis that can withstand ongoing geopolitical pressure. Russian President Vladimir Putin’s advisor Nikolai Patrushev’s recent visit to China points to something more consequential than another round of Russia-China strategic rhetoric: Moscow is trying to turn maritime cooperation with Beijing into infrastructure, technology and logistics that can survive geopolitical pressure.

articles.title: Brazilian Amazon deforestation falls to lowest on record as pivotal vote looms
articles.summary: Brazilian Amazon deforestation hit its lowest recorded level since 1988, according to new government data. This decline marks a significant policy win for President Lula ahead of the 25 October presidential run-off. The sustainability of this progress remains uncertain as voters choose between candidates with diverging environmental stances. The election outcome will directly determine whether these conservation gains hold or reverse.

articles.title: No 10 leaves option open to impose Chinese EV tariffs if UK joins EU scheme
articles.summary: Downing Street confirmed the UK may impose tariffs on Chinese electric vehicles if it joins the EU's Made in Europe package. Beijing warned the measure would be discriminatory. France dropped its opposition to British participation in the scheme. The decision remains pending final negotiations. Beijing warns against ‘discriminatory’ step after France drops opposition to British role in Made in Europe packageNo 10 has left the door open to imposing tariffs on Chinese-made electric vehicles as part of the Made in Europe package, prompting a warning from Beijing that such a move would be “discriminatory”. Downing Street said on Friday that it would “welcome the objective to have the UK inclu.

articles.title: Russia Still Needs More Soldiers. The Kremlin Is Still Desperate To Avoid Mobilization
articles.summary: Russia continues quiet mobilization to replace losses in Ukraine. The Kremlin avoided a formal national draft order after recent elections. Coercive recruiting tactics persist across the country. Military forces remain depleted despite ongoing combat operations. Many Russians feared the Kremlin would order a new mobilization after last month’s elections: to replenish decimated forces fighting in Ukraine. That hasn’t happened. But creative and coercive recruiting tactics – called “quiet” or “creeping” mobilization by some – continue nationwide.

articles.title: Sudan’s war spreads as drones and hunger take a deadly toll
articles.summary: Drone strikes are killing civilians across El Obeid and Blue Nile. Famine risk is spreading through Darfur and Kordofan. The Security Council met to address the world's largest hunger and displacement crisis. Ambassadors pressed for a ceasefire, safe aid access, and a halt to weapons flows. As drone strikes kill civilians from El Obeid to Blue Nile and famine risk spreads across Darfur and Kordofan, the Security Council meets on Sudan – the world’s largest hunger and displacement crisis.

articles.title: Russia's Shadow War On NATO Is 'Bound To Intensify'
articles.summary: Russia's shadow war against NATO involves drone incursions, sabotage, and assassination attempts. Christopher Walker of the Center for European Policy Analysis says the campaign is approaching a crucial point. The strategy has largely backfired by drawing a resolute response. He predicts the conflict will continue to intensify. Russia's shadow campaign of drone incursions, sabotage, and assassination attempts in NATO countries has largely backfired by drawing a resolute response but is approaching a "crucial point," Christopher Walker, vice president of the Center for European Policy Analysis, tells RFE/RL.

articles.title: Hot US inflation singes Asia as higher-for-longer Fed rates loom
articles.summary: September US inflation hit 3.7% year-on-year, exceeding forecasts. The data suggests the Federal Reserve will keep interest rates higher for longer. Asian markets face renewed pressure on currencies, capital flows, and economic growth from this sustained monetary tightening. TOKYO. An unwelcome blast of US inflation is blowing across Asia’s markets. September’s hotter-than-expected price data revived concerns that the Federal Reserve will keep rates higher for longer, threatening fresh pressure on currencies, capital flows and economic growth across the region.

articles.title: Zelenskyy Says US Diesel Deal Will Put Money 'Straight Into Putin's Pocket'
articles.summary: Nine US senators requested an investigation into satellite system disruptions affecting Ukraine’s military. The bipartisan group acted as European officials rallied around Kyiv. This occurred after President Trump again criticized Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy during the EU summit. A bipartisan group of nine US senators has called for an investigation into disruptions to satellite systems supporting Ukraine's military as European officials rallied around Kyiv after President Donald Trump again attacked his Ukrainian counterpart Volodymyr Zelenskyy.

articles.title: Rubio Heads To Central Asia As US Seeks Bigger Role In Region Dominated By Russia, China
articles.summary: Marco Rubio travels to Uzbekistan to meet with five Central Asian nations. The Trump administration aims to strengthen commercial ties and expand US strategic presence. The region has historically been dominated by Russian and Chinese influence. US Secretary of State Marco Rubio heads to Uzbekistan this weekend for talks with five Central Asian countries as the Trump administration seeks to strengthen commercial ties and expand Washington's strategic presence in the region.

articles.title: Tech market sell-off deepens amid fears over US inflation and AI debt
articles.summary: Global tech markets suffered a deep sell-off driven by inflation fears and AI sector debt. Shares in Samsung and SoftBank plunged as traders worried about potential interest rate hikes. The decline reflects growing anxiety over the heavy borrowing underpinning current artificial intelligence infrastructure. Chip makers and tech investors such as Samsung and SoftBank plunge as potential interest rate hikes spook marketsBusiness news – live updatesLarry Elliott: the global economy is muddling through.

articles.title: Afghanistan faces record hunger levels amid rampant rights violations
articles.summary: Afghanistan faces record hunger levels with 15.9 million people facing acute food insecurity. A global hunger monitor report released Thursday confirmed these are the highest levels ever recorded. Conditions are expected to worsen significantly in the coming months due to ongoing rights violations. Acute malnutrition and hunger in Afghanistan have reached the highest levels ever recorded, with 15.9 million people facing acute food insecurity and conditions set to worsen in the coming months, according to a global hunger monitor report released on Thursday.

articles.title: The world is waging a ‘war on nature’ as progress on biodiversity targets lags
articles.summary: The UN warns fewer than half of national biodiversity targets are on track. This report arrives days before the COP17 conference in Yerevan, Armenia. The assessment highlights a significant gap in global efforts to protect plants, animals, and ecosystems from further degradation. Fewer than half of the national targets set to protect the world’s plants, animals and ecosystems are on track, the UN warns in a new report, days before countries gather in Yerevan, Armenia, for the COP17 biodiversity conference.

articles.title: AI, green energy and economic transitions risk leaving vulnerable communities behind, UN warns
articles.summary: A new UN report warns that rapid economic shifts risk leaving vulnerable communities behind. Artificial intelligence and renewable energy transitions are reshaping global economies. These changes create new opportunities but also threaten to deepen socio-economic inequalities. The report highlights the need for inclusive policy frameworks. Rapid transformations – from artificial intelligence and digital technologies to renewable energy and demographic shifts – are reshaping economies worldwide, creating new opportunities but also threatening to deepen socio-economic inequalities, a new UN report warned on Thursday.

articles.title: LGBTQ+ people go into hiding in Senegal as hundreds are arrested
articles.summary: Senegal authorities detained more than 320 LGBTQ+ individuals since February after the government tightened its law criminalising homosexuality. The arrests triggered forced HIV testing and limited access to legal representation, according to a Human Rights Watch report. The crackdown signals a broader clamp At least 320 people detained for ‘acts against nature’ after law criminalising homosexuality toughened, HRW reportsMass arrests, forced HIV testing and barriers to legal representation are part of an escalating crackdown against LGBTQ+ people in Senegal, according to a new report. More than 320 individuals have been arrested and detained on allegations of “acts against nature” since February, accor.

articles.title: Indonesia fights fire with dry ice as toxic haze spreads across region
articles.summary: Indonesia is testing dry ice dispersal in South Sumatra. The government deployed planes to combat toxic haze. This follows failed cloud seeding attempts. Regional neighbors remain angry over the smoke. Having tried cloud seeding and water bombing, one pilot project will see dry ice dispersed by plane across the province of South SumatraAs fires ravage Indonesia, emitting a toxic smoke that has drawn the ire of regional neighbours, the government is testing an unusual new approach to tackle the haze: dry ice. Having tried cloud seeding, water bombing and sending in army personnel to fight the fire.
